content.text: Option A offers the lowest operational overhead but requires significant code changes for idempotency and has vendor lock-in. Option B provides advanced queuing features but comes with an unknown operational cost due to lack of team experience. Option C offers strong transactional guarantees for billing-related jobs but risks impacting the primary database's performance, especially during month-end.

snapshot.content: Analysis · Cost Implications at Higher Volume

content.text: At three times the current volume, the managed cloud queue's infrastructure cost would rise to approximately $900, making the self-hosted broker a more cost-effective option at higher volumes, as its infrastructure cost would remain flat.

ai.stableNodeKey: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Costs § text#1

content.text: Option C was load-tested on a staging database copy using synthetic jobs. It achieved 1,200 jobs/minute with a p95 claim latency of 18 ms. At 2,000 jobs/minute, primary CPU reached 85%, and p95 latency increased to 240 ms. These results may not be directly transferable to production due to the staging environment's smaller size (one-quarter of production) and the untested 1,800 jobs/minute scenario.
